page: Amazon Web Services m6i.large is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features a dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at 3.5 GHz, configured with 2 virtual CPUs derived from 1 physical core via simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 8.0 GB of DDR4 clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual core. Hardware capabilities include AVX, AVX-512 (Foundation and VNNI), and cryptographic acceleration extensions such as AES and SHA-NI.

The instance does not include bundled local instance storage, requiring attached network storage such as EBS for persistent data. Network performance provides a baseline throughput of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. The configuration contains no dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate average single-threaded compute performance, with stress-ng single-core reaching 1804.09 and Geekbench single-core registering 1543.0. Compression and decompression tests, including gzip and bzip3, align within the middle 50% tier. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks reflect the physical ceiling of a single dual-threaded core, placing stress-ng multi-core (1919.97), Geekbench multi-core (1806.0), and PassMark CPU (2909.32) in the lower performance brackets. Memory bandwidth under large block read and write conditions measures 13.81 GB/sec and 12.92 GB/sec respectively.

The m6i.large functions as an economical tier for predictable low-concurrency operations where dedicated Intel execution is required without large parallel core counts. Workload fit is oriented toward microservices, lightweight web servers, API gateways, background workers, and staging environments.
description: Amazon Web Services m6i.large is a general-purpose instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring 2 vCPUs from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. It includes 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory, providing a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio suitable for general compute tasks. The instance carries no bundled local storage, requiring external block storage, and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without GPU acceleration. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance yields average single-core performance while multi-core metrics reflect its dual-vCPU design constraints. Equipped with AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions, the m6i.large offers a cost-effective platform for low-density microservices, lightweight backend APIs, staging servers, and modest general-purpose application workloads.
